run.question:
Alertmanager alert KubePodCrashLooping (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/kube-prometheus-stack-kube-state-metrics since 2026-11-26T07:32:09Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The KubePodCrashLooping alert is explained by a spec change to Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog: its container template now runs command ["cta", "/etc/hosts"], so every new container instance fails at exec time with 'exec: "cta": executable file not found in $PATH' and never starts. Pod product-catalog-57c46774f7-6z5ff (created 07:31:30Z on ReplicaSet product-catalog-57c46774f7) has 6 restarts, ready=false, waiting reason RunContainerError/CrashLoopBackOff, last termination reason StartError with exit code 128, and kubelet Failed/BackOff events; the Deployment holds replicas 2 / ready 1 / unavailable 1 with Progressing=True (ReplicaSetUpdated). The change appears in the Deployment's managedFields as an Update by manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 07:31:30Z, the same second the new ReplicaSet was scaled up; no other otel-demo Deployment has a non-helm writer, and no chaos/fault-injection webhook was found among the mutating webhook configurations. The flagd feature flags are all 'off', so the productCatalogFailure/productCatalogLockContention scenarios are rejected as the cause of the exec failure. Impact stays with this pod and its Deployment: the previous pod product-catalog-658dcdbc87-nmbh4 is Ready with 0 restarts and remains the single ready endpoint of Service product-catalog, product-catalog span calls kept flowing at ~18/s with no ERROR status series returned for it, and a cluster-wide pod scan found this as the only container with a waiting reason or restarts. Who or what issued the Deployment patch cannot be established: change history is not integrated, and a cluster-wide ConfigMap name search for fault/chaos/inject/cta/experiment returned no_data rather than a usable negative.

claims.text: Pod product-catalog-57c46774f7-6z5ff in namespace otel-demo (created 07:31:30Z, owner ReplicaSet product-catalog-57c46774f7) has container 'product-catalog' not ready with restartCount 6; its state is waiting reason RunContainerError with message 'failed to create containerd task: ... exec: "cta": executable file not found in $PATH', and its lastState.terminated shows reason StartError, exitCode 128, finishedAt 2026-11-26T07:37:07Z.

kubelet events on pod product-catalog-57c46774f7-6z5ff record 7 occurrences of reason Failed/type Warning with message 'Error: failed to create containerd task: ... exec: "cta": executable file not found in $PATH' between 07:31:32Z and 07:37:07Z, plus 9 occurrences of reason BackOff 'Back-off restarting failed container product-catalog in pod product-catalog-57c46774f7-6z5ff'.

Both the pod spec of product-catalog-57c46774f7-6z5ff and the current Deployment product-catalog container template set containers[product-catalog].command to ["cta","/etc/hosts"] with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-product-catalog, while the older ReplicaSet product-catalog-658dcdbc87 (created 07:24:06Z, owner Deployment product-catalog) has command null and its pod is Ready with 0 restarts.

Deployment product-catalog metadata.managedFieldsSummary shows helm Apply at 07:24:03Z followed by an Update by manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 07:31:30Z (annotation deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=2); within the same otel-demo namespace, all other 25 Deployments list only helm and kube-controller-manager as writers, i.e. product-catalog is the only deployment patched after the initial helm install.

Deployment product-catalog scaled up ReplicaSet product-catalog-57c46774f7 at 07:31:30Z (event reason ScalingReplicaSet, message 'Scaled up replica set product-catalog-57c46774f7 from 0 to 1'); all other otel-demo deployments show only their initial 07:24:0xZ scale-up event.

Deployment product-catalog status at query time: replicas 2, readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1, updatedReplicas 1, condition Progressing=True with reason ReplicaSetUpdated ('ReplicaSet "product-catalog-57c46774f7" is progressing') and Available=True.

kube-state-metrics confirms the alerting series at 07:37:23Z: kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="otel-demo",pod="product-catalog-57c46774f7-6z5ff",container="product-catalog"}=6 and kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{...,reason="RunContainerError"}=1, both carrying job="kube-prometheus-stack", service="kube-prometheus-stack-kube-state-metrics", uid="78f10211-f4f3-442c-866b-e2089a5c11ac" — i.e. the alert's 'service' label is the kube-state-metrics scrape target, while the affected workload is pod/Deployment product-catalog.

A cluster-wide scan of all 69 pods at 07:38:18Z found exactly one container with a non-empty waiting reason or a nonzero restart count: pod product-catalog-57c46774f7-6z5ff, reason CrashLoopBackOff, restarts 6.

Endpoints of Service product-catalog list ready address 10.244.2.90 (targetRef pod product-catalog-658dcdbc87-nmbh4) and notReadyAddress 10.244.1.160 (targetRef pod product-catalog-57c46774f7-6z5ff), so the service still has one serving backend while the new pod is excluded.

product-catalog showed no error-status spans and no drop in span activity: the only returned status_code for traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="product-catalog"} is STATUS_CODE_UNSET (increase 13432.05 over 65m), its 5m rate is 0 at 07:27:09Z then 18.29 and 18.35 spans/s at 07:32:09Z and 07:37:09Z, and product-catalog does not appear in the per-service STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase, unlike frontend (72), frontend-proxy (31), load-generator (20), agent (8), accounting (1).

The crashlooping container produced no application output: fetch_pod_logs for product-catalog-57c46774f7-6z5ff read 0 lines from container product-catalog (current and previous instances) and 1 line from init container wait-for-astronomy-db ('astronomy-db (10.96.229.220:5432) open', 07:31:31Z), consistent with a failure before process start rather than an application crash.

Rejected: a flagd feature-flag fault (e.g. productCatalogFailure or productCatalogLockContention) causing product-catalog failures. ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config ('demo.flagd.json') has defaultVariant "off" for every flag, including productCatalogFailure and productCatalogLockContention, and the observed failure is an exec error before the container process starts, which feature flags cannot produce.

Rejected: admission-time mutation of the pod container command by a chaos/fault-injection webhook. The three mutatingwebhookconfigurations present (cert-manager-webhook, kube-prometheus-stack-admission, opentelemetry-operator-mutation, whose mpod.kb.io webhook only targets opentelemetry.io/v1alpha1 Instrumentation objects) contain no rule on core v1 Pods that rewrites container commands, and the only non-helm writer observed on the product-catalog Deployment is the API client recorded as manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 07:31:30Z.

No other otel-demo workload shows pod-level distress: of the 27 pods present in otel-demo, all except product-catalog-57c46774f7-6z5ff are Running with Ready=True and restartCount 0, including the surviving product-catalog pod product-catalog-658dcdbc87-nmbh4 (running since 07:24:10Z, 0 restarts).

No event in the authorized window names a chaos/fault-injection object: events across all namespaces grouped by involvedObject kind/namespace/reason (excluding Certificate/CertificateRequest/Pod) contain only Certificate-related, Deployment/ReplicaSet ScalingReplicaSet/SuccessfulCreate, Job, Lease, PVC, PDB, Service, StatefulSet, ClickHouseInstallation and OpenTelemetryCollector reasons; the only Deployment groups outside otel-demo are the platform namespaces itbench-mcp-servers, itbench-observability, itbench-operators, itbench-system, kube-system, nginx-gateway and opencost.

Hypothesis (supported by the spec diff and the deterministic exec error, but the issuing actor is unidentified): the Deployment product-catalog was patched at 07:31:30Z by an external API client (managedFields manager 'OpenAPI-Generator') to set container command ["cta","/etc/hosts"]; the Deployment controller rolled out ReplicaSet product-catalog-57c46774f7 whose pod cannot exec 'cta', producing RunContainerError/CrashLoopBackOff and the KubePodCrashLooping alert at 07:32:09Z, while the rollout is stuck because the new pod never becomes ready.

Background errors unrelated to this cause: cumulative STATUS_CODE_ERROR span counts from 07:26:09Z to 07:36:09Z are flat at frontend 72, frontend-proxy 31, load-generator 20, agent 8, accounting 1, and ad, flagd, fraud-detection, payment and recommendation first produce an ERROR-status series only at 07:36:09Z with value 0; none of these services is product-catalog.

gaps: Change history is not integrated, so which user/client/pipeline (only the managedFields manager name 'OpenAPI-Generator' is visible) patched Deployment product-catalog at 07:31:30Z and why cannot be determined.

The cluster-wide search for ConfigMaps whose names match fault|chaos|inject|cta|experiment returned no_data (not ok, 54 ConfigMaps processed, no matches returned), so a ConfigMap-held fault setting for this workload could be neither confirmed nor excluded by that query.
The customresourcedefinitions inventory could not be read (RESULT_TOO_LARGE on every attempt), so a CRD-based fault-injection object holding a 'cta' setting cannot be excluded.
ConfigMap itbench-observability/kubernetes-topology-collector-98c67e01 was written at 07:25:08Z by manager 'manager'; its content and purpose were not examined and it is not tied to this cause.
No product-catalog container logs exist (current and previous instances read 0 lines) because the container never started, so no application-side diagnostic is available from the failing container.

Jaeger trace detail for service product-catalog ends at 07:24:41Z (source window 07:24:10-07:24:41) and the 06:32-07:37 traces_search exceeded the view limit, so span-level detail of the 07:31Z-07:37Z period is unavailable; span-level claims rest on Prometheus span metrics only.

The origin of the small ERROR-status span counts that appear for ad, flagd, fraud-detection, payment and recommendation near 07:36-07:37Z is unknown and was not investigated further; those services show no pod-level failure.
next_steps: Verify with the owner of the fault-injection/test harness what patch was sent to Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog at 2026-11-26T07:31:30Z (managedFields manager 'OpenAPI-Generator').

If the injected command was not intended, restore the helm-managed template for Deployment product-catalog (container command unset) and re-run the rollout so ReplicaSet product-catalog-57c46774f7 is replaced and the CrashLoopBackOff pod is removed.
After the fix, confirm kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total for the replacement pod stays at 0 and Deployment product-catalog reports unavailableReplicas 0.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
